newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland wants zloty externally convertible in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Poland wants zloty externally convertible in 1998.

text.p: Poland wants to introduce external convertibility of the zloty through a new currency law expected to be in place in early 1998, a senior central bank official said on Friday.

"The law will establish the principle that the zloty can be used as a settlement currency outside Poland," Michal Krakowiak, head of the National Bank of Poland's currency department, told a banking seminar.
The zloty can now be used as a means of settlement only inside Poland although it can be freely exchanged for other currencies.

He said the bill, now prepared by the finance ministry and the central bank, would also increase to the status of a law an existing regulation that frees currency accounts and capital flows in line with Poland's OECD entry agreement. @
"We introduce a general rule that there is freedom in current account transfers and capital flows," he said.
Krakowiak said the bill would probably include a so-called negative list of types of capital transactions that would still require central bank approval.
